ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP and sanctions screening for all directors, officers, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against FINTRAC requirements, Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, US OFAC SDN List, and UK HM Treasury Consolidated Sanctions List. Enhanced due diligence applies on any positive match, change in ownership, or adverse open-source intelligence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names using Latin script and an English-language name are required. Foreign-script names require certified transliteration into Latin characters. The name must be distinctive, not confusingly similar to existing BC corporate or extraprovincial registrations, and must not mislead the public as to geographic scope or regulated business activities.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar of Companies via BC Corporate Online within 30 days, providing legal arguments and evidence of distinctiveness and absence of confusion. If reconsideration is refused, the applicant may file a judicial review or statutory appeal with the Supreme Court of British Columbia.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this industry. A BC street-address service and a registered agent accepting legal service are sufficient. The registered office must be open during normal business hours and records must be available for inspection; day-to-day operational management may be overseas.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, approximately 3% annualized probability for this low-risk PR-agency classification absent adverse AML/CFT indicators. Probability increases materially upon FINTRAC notice, CRA audit selection, or registrar compliance review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: British Columbia Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57 — sections 1(1) (unlimited liability company definition), 10 (incorporation application), 21-24 (corporate names), 51-53 (articles and notice of articles), 57 (certificate of incorporation), 173 (directors); Business Corporations Regulation, B.C. Reg. 42/2004.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies — British Columbia Corporate Registry, BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance, Victoria, British Columbia.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1), Notice of Articles (Form 2), and Certificate of Incorporation (Form 3) under B.C. Reg. 42/2004.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the BC BCA. Shares may be issued without par value for such consideration as the board determines. No government escrow account is required for subscription proceeds; funds must be deposited into the company's bank account and may not be withdrawn except by lawful dividend, permitted return of capital, or other valid corporate distribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the share subscriptions listed in the subscribers' register be accepted and, effective as of incorporation, 100 common no-par-value shares are allotted and issued to the founding subscriber for CAD 1.00 per share, fully paid, and the share certificate book is approved. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be fixed at Suite 1000, 555 West Georgia Street, Vancouver, British Columbia, V6B 1M1, and that the records office be established at that same address. RESOLVED that the following individuals be appointed officers of the Company: [Name], President; [Name], Secretary-Treasurer. Any one officer is authorized, jointly with the President, to open banking accounts, execute banking mandates, and complete all statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry — Name Approval Unit, BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Online / BC OnePass portal).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through the BC Registries Corporate Online portal. Run a name search against the BC corporate register and the federal NUANS database to confirm availability. Include a distinctive element and the mandatory legal element 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', or 'ULC'. Retain the reservation number, valid for 56 days. If the exact name is unavailable, file a supplementary name request with an alternate distinctive element.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of CAD 30 name reservation fee
Proposed Articles showing legal element for ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, request written reasons from the registrar, file a revised name reservation with a new distinctive element within the 56-day validity period, or seek review under section 24 of the BC Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application, Notice of Articles, and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Corporate Registry — online incorporation filing service (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form 1 (Incorporation Application) and Form 2 (Notice of Articles) online. Attach the executed Articles incorporating the unlimited liability company designation and a share structure permitting shares without par value. State a physical registered office and records office address within British Columbia (no post office box). List the first directors; BC law imposes no Canadian residency requirement. Pay the CAD 350 incorporation filing fee and receive the registrar's acknowledgement.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation with ULC designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues an objection or deficiency notice, cure the defect (e.g., correct the registered office address or director consents) and re-file an amended application or Notice of Articles within 30 days. Where an error appears in the issued certificate, apply for a corrected certificate under section 267 of the BCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and Company Records Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry (Registrar of Companies) for certificate issuance; company corporate secretary for records book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download and print the authenticated Certificate of Incorporation (Form 3) issued by the registrar. Verify the registration number, incorporation date, and legal name. Establish the corporate minute book containing the share ledger, register of directors, register of officers, and records of the registered and records offices. Stamp and bind the Articles and Notice of Articles as filed.
required_dossiers: Filed Notice of Articles (Form 2), PDF version
Articles endorsed with the filing date
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical or legal-element error, request a corrected certificate from the registrar under section 267 of the BCA within 90 days. If the records book is incomplete, rectify the deficiency internally by filing the omitted register pages and obtaining board ratification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency — Business Registration Online (BRO) and CRA Vancouver Tax Services Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register online with CRA BRO using the provincial incorporation data. Obtain the nine-digit Business Number (BN) and the required program accounts: corporate income tax account (RC0001), GST/HST account (RT0001) where annual worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000, and payroll account (RP0001) upon hiring employees. Verify that the authorized representative and director identification match the BC registry records.
required_dossiers: Bank account details for direct deposit
Estimated revenue and GST/HST threshold declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN application is rejected or deferred, reconcile the data mismatch with the BC Corporate Registry, obtain an updated corrected notice, and re-submit through CRA BRO. For GST/HST, request retroactive registration effective the date of first taxable supply if the threshold is exceeded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Organizational Matters and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and corporate secretary (private action; no public registry filing required).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold or pass by written consent the first board meeting in accordance with section 175 of the BCA. Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution covering allotment of shares, fixing of the registered office and records office, and appointment of officers. Execute share certificates, receive subscription funds into the corporate bank account, approve the corporate seal, and sign banking resolutions and wire transfer mandates.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution (written consent in lieu of meeting)
Share subscription agreement and payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct defective board resolutions by a subsequent unanimous written board resolution ratifying prior actions nunc pro tunc. Improperly issued shares may be validated by re-allotment and board ratification, or by an application to court where statutory validation is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Municipal, WorkSafeBC, and Annual Registry Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Vancouver Business Licensing Office; BC Corporate Registry (annual report); WorkSafeBC.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a City of Vancouver general business licence for the office-based public relations agency. Register the employer account with WorkSafeBC if employees are resident in BC. File the initial BC annual report within 60 days after the incorporation anniversary and thereafter annually online, confirming directors, registered office, and records office. No sector-specific provincial operating licence applies to ISIC 7310 public relations services.
required_dossiers: City of Vancouver business licence application and lease proof
BC annual report filing and fee payment
Notice of Articles for municipal verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late or deficient annual reports may be reinstated by filing the completed return and paying the applicable late fee. Municipal licence objections may be cured by submitting supplementary lease, occupancy, or zoning evidence within 21 days. WorkSafeBC registration deficiencies are remedied by self-corrected online filing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no province-wide industrial licence exists for ISIC 7310 (international media relations and crisis PR). Regulatory oversight is limited to municipal business licensing (City of Vancouver Business Licence Office) and general provincial workplace safety jurisdiction (WorkSafeBC).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: City of Vancouver Business Licence — 'Business – Administrative Office' classification. No sector-specific provincial operating permit is required for public relations or communications consultancy services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy — Environmental Assessment Office (EAO)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based PR activity is not a reviewable project under the Environmental Assessment Act, S.B.C. 2018, c. 51 or the Reviewable Projects Regulation, and triggers no Schedule B physical activity or industrial facility designation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no point-source industrial wastewater discharge permit under section 6 of the Environmental Management Act, S.B.C. 2003, c. 53; no VOC emission thresholds; no dangerous waste registration under the Hazardous Waste Regulation, B.C. Reg. 63/88. Office waste must comply with City of Vancouver Solid Waste Bylaw No. 8417, and any future physical printing or materials handling would be subject to municipal sewer limits under Sewer and Watercourse Bylaw No. 8093.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification obtained through Vancouver Fire Rescue Services inspection under the BC Fire Code, B.C. Reg. 238/2021 (fire alarms, extinguishers, and egress). WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance and employer registration under the Workers Compensation Act and OHS Regulation, B.C. Reg. 296/97 (Part 3). Structural load inspection certificate from a BC-licensed professional engineer for Class B/C office occupancy under the BC Building Code. No separate civil defense approval applies to standard leasehold office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – federal corporate income tax and GST/HST; British Columbia Ministry of Finance – BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) and provincial corporate income tax (administered federally by CRA). Digital portals: CRA My Business Account, CRA Business Registration Online (BRO), and BC eTaxBC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the BC Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC) under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) through BC Corporate Online; obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and corporate registry number. Step 2: Register the corporation with CRA through Business Registration Online (BRO) to obtain the nine-digit Business Number (BN) and federal program accounts: RT (corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST), RP (payroll) as needed, and RM (import/export) as needed; the BN is the Canadian tax identification number (TIN) for both federal and BC corporate income tax, because BC corporate income tax is collected and administered by CRA. Step 3: Register separately for BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) under the Provincial Sales Tax Act via eTaxBC or the BC Ministry of Finance; the PST account number is separate from the CRA BN. Step 4: For a ULC whose primary activity is overseas PR communications, register for GST/HST voluntarily even if below the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold in order to claim input tax credits (ITCs) and to zero-rate export services. No minimum share capital is required and non-resident ownership is permitted; a BC registered office and at least one director are required under provincial law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not maintain a check-the-box election for domestic tax purposes. A BC ULC is a separate taxable Canadian corporation resident in Canada, subject to Part I federal income tax and BC provincial corporate income tax on worldwide income. The unlimited liability capital structure allows U.S. members to elect pass-through treatment under U.S. check-the-box regulations (Treas. Reg. §301.7701-3) by filing Form 8832; however, Canadian tax law continues to treat the ULC as a corporation. Hybrid mismatch adjustments (Income Tax Act ss.18.2, 18.3, 18.4, 20.03 and Canadian implementation of the OECD Hybrid Mismatch recommendations) may disallow deductions or withhold taxes on certain cross-border payments and should be reviewed when structuring pass-through elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST). BC does not participate in the HST; a taxable supply in BC generally bears 5% GST and may bear 7% PST if the particular service or good is PST-taxable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies in any calendar quarter or trailing four quarters; once exceeded, the ULC must register and collect GST/HST. BC PST: no general economic-turnover threshold; any seller making taxable sales of PST-assessable goods or services in British Columbia is required to register, while a non-resident PR firm supplying zero-rated services to overseas clients will not have Canadian PST nexus if no tangible property or enumerated services are supplied in BC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no national real-time e-invoicing clearance regime, no mandated interoperable B2B e-invoicing API, and no digital fiscal stamping system. GST/HST registrants are required to file returns electronically through CRA's GST/HST NETFILE, EDI, or My Business Account and to remit net tax by the statutory monthly/quarterly deadlines. BC PST returns are filed electronically through eTaxBC. No government pre-approval of invoices is required, but CRA may verify invoices and supporting evidence during audit; registrants must maintain books and records containing all particulars of zero-rated export supplies, including copies of invoices, contracts, and outward remittance evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A BC ULC providing international media relations, crisis public relations, and overseas PR communication services may zero-rate its supplies for GST/HST under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, section 7 when the supply is made to a non-resident person (i) who is not registered for GST/HST and is not acquiring the service for consumption, use, or supply in Canada, and (ii) when the service is not performed in connection with real or tangible personal property situated in Canada. The agency should obtain a written declaration of non-residency, a valid OECD tax-residency certificate or equivalent, and contractual terms confirming the overseas-client engagement. Any services that relate to media targeting in Canada, are rendered for a Canadian resident, or are provided to a Canadian GST/HST registrant will be taxable at 5% GST (plus BC PST if separately assessable).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A / Canada Export Declaration) – required solely where tangible marketing assets, printed media materials, or merchandise are physically exported as part of PR campaign deliverables
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / courier waybill for physical exports
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT payment or bank confirmation of remittance of fees from overseas clients
Executed master services agreement and zero-rated invoices identifying the non-resident client, service scope, and statutory zero-rating basis under ETA Schedule VI Part V s.7
Certificate of Residence / OECD tax-residency certificate of the overseas recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: A claim of export zero-rating is subject to strict documentary scrutiny. If the ULC fails to satisfy the ETA export conditions, CRA may reassess the supplies as taxable at 5% GST (collectible on the gross consideration), deny associated input tax credits, and claw back any GST/HST refunds already credited. In cases of negligence, ETA s.285(1) imposes a penalty of the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of any net tax under-assessed or over-claimed; s.280 and s.281 add daily compound interest for arrears and refund reassessments. Fraudulent claims can be reassessed beyond the normal four-year limitation period and may lead to criminal prosecution under ETA s.238 and Income Tax Act s.327, with fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and/or imprisonment for up to five years, in addition to provincial administrative penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); bank chartering and prudential regulation are administered by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), while anti-money laundering supervision is administered by FINTRAC. Canada has no separate foreign-exchange-control agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada provides full current and capital account convertibility and has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations. Dividends, management fees, royalties and branch profits may be freely repatriated, subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax, corporate solvency law, and standard escrow/contractual restrictions. For a BC ULC, no exchange-control approval or conversion permit is required; the practical hurdles are banking KYC, source-of-funds proof, and any intercompany transfer pricing/withholding issues.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose a statutory surrender requirement, forced conversion ratio, or mandatory repatriation timeline for export proceeds or cross-border service revenues such as public relations retainers. Foreign-currency receivables may be retained in Canadian or offshore accounts, but deferred repatriation and passive foreign-currency holdings must be reviewed for CRA foreign accrual property income and transfer pricing exposure.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditional Medium-Low. Offshore digital EMIs are not authorized to accept deposits or operate as Schedule I banks in Canada and are not a compliant primary treasury rail for a BC ULC. A foreign EMI may be used only as an ancillary payment channel if it is properly licensed in its home jurisdiction and, where applicable, registered with FINTRAC or licensed under Canada's Retail Payment Activities Act. Primary liquidity, client escrow, and capital receipts must be held with a Canadian chartered bank to preserve CDIC-protected settlement and clean corporate audit trails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute statutory mandate requires physical attendance, and FINTRAC permits remote identity verification using approved two-factor or credential-based methods. In practice, however, major Canadian banks usually require a live video interview with at least one director or authorized signatory for a non-resident-owned ULC, and many banks still require in-person notarization or a branch interview. The practical mandate is Medium: remote onboarding is possible with enhanced due diligence, but Canadian counsel sponsorship or a director's presence in Vancouver materially accelerates account approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners and pass-through ULC structure flagged for source-of-funds verification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBC/BC notice of articles, memorandum and articles, bylaws, register of directors, full organizational chart to natural persons, board resolution authorizing account opening, current passports, source-of-wealth statement, parent company financials or audited statements, and CRA business number / tax-residency confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border retainer receipts from related or overseas clients lacking visible underlying commercial activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master services agreements and scopes of work, invoices referencing ISIC 7310 services, payment schedules, beneficiary contracts, client references, operational-evidence file (BC office lease, staff expense records, performance reports), and CRA transfer pricing documentation where related-party payments exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PR/media communications activities incorrectly characterized as money services business or unlicensed payment processing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from Canadian counsel confirming the entity holds no client funds and does not act as a payment intermediary; express contractual language delimiting public relations, media relations, and crisis communications only; no commission, custody, FX dealing, or value-transfer activity; FINTRAC/MSB non-registration position; and a transaction-flow diagram showing client-to-ULC-to-vendor retainers as service payments, not payment aggregation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: BC ULC unlimited liability structure generating enhanced due diligence on corporate veil and creditor exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Explanatory memorandum on ULC legal characteristics, BC registry good-standing certificate, unlimited liability indemnity insurance or shareholder indemnity agreement, corporate insurance confirmation, audited or reviewed financial statements, and shareholder agreement evidencing lawful commercial purpose and financial capacity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons, foreign-government-linked clients, or high-risk jurisdiction payment flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP self-declaration, beneficial-ownership attestation, source-of-funds declarations, senior management/AML committee approval, sanctions and adverse-media screening reports, detailed client onboarding files with contractual purpose, and third-party due diligence on all high-risk counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital may be injected freely as equity subscription or shareholder loan without exchange-control approval. For equity, the ULC must issue shares under the BC Business Corporations Act and may use a share subscription agreement and board resolution; for debt, a formal shareholder loan agreement with market-rate interest and transfer pricing support is required. Wire instructions must use SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the remitting bank to the Canadian bank's correspondent, with the receiving ULC legal name, account number, and Field 70 reference such as 'ULC_SH_CAP' or 'ULC_SH_LOAN'. The receiving Canadian bank should be pre-notified with the board resolution, source-of-funds evidence, organizational chart, and beneficial-ownership declarations. CAD credits are cleared through Canada's Large Value Transfer System; USD credits are cleared through CHIPS/Fedwire via the bank's U.S. correspondent. No statutory waiting period or surrender requirement applies.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payments to vendors, freelancers, photographers, media platforms, and international PR offices, use SWIFT MT103 for every single-beneficiary cross-border disbursement; when an intermediate correspondent consumes cover, use MT202 COVER for USD settlement. Commercial Letters of Credit are permissible but are not necessary for service-based public relations disbursements; a clean SWIFT MT103 with invoices and contracts is the standard rail. Domestic CAD vendor payments should be routed via the Automated Clearing Settlement System or Real-Time Rail, while cross-border CAD/USD payments use the SWIFT network and LVTS/CHIPS. The treasury file for each payment should contain contract, invoice, sanctions screen (UN/EU/OFAC), and beneficial-owner certification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards on CAD/USD and CAD/EUR
Non-deliverable forwards (structurally permissible for exotic pairs, though CAD is fully convertible and deliverable forwards are the standard instrument)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registry (Registrar of Companies), Province of British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after each anniversary date of the company's incorporation or registration in British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years may lead to administrative strike-off or dissolution; late reinstatement requires a court order under section 342 of the BC Business Corporations Act and payment of additional fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal) plus supporting financial statements and schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of any unpaid balance plus 1% per full month of delinquency up to 12 months; repeated failure may trigger gross-negligence penalties and criminal sanctions under the Income Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (if the company is a GST/HST registrant under the Excise Tax Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within three months after the end of the fiscal year for annual filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or remit attracts a penalty of 5% of the unremitted amount plus interest accruing daily; continued non-compliance may result in asset seizure or director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue, asset, or employee threshold under the BC Business Corporations Act for a private British Columbia unlimited liability corporation (ULC). The company must appoint an auditor at its annual general meeting unless all shareholders, including non-voting shareholders, unanimously waive the appointment in respect of that financial year. Publicly accountable enterprises and entities otherwise prescribed by law require a mandatory independent audit. The Canada Revenue Agency may also require audited financial statements in the course of an income tax audit or assessment dispute.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the CPA Canada Handbook; IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises and ASPE for private entities. The BC ULC may report under ASPE when an audit is waived or where shareholders elect private-enterprise accounting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For a British Columbia unlimited liability corporation, there is no separate annual beneficial-ownership confirmation filing to the BC Registrar. The annual report only confirms directors and registered office information. Share transfers must be promptly recorded in the company's Register of Members, maintained at the registered office, before being reflected in company records and available for authorized inspection. Director changes must be reported to the BC Registrar by filing a Notice of Change of Directors within 14 days of the change. If the ULC is also registered under any federal act, additional beneficial-ownership reporting obligations may apply, but a purely provincial BC ULC does not file a UBO return annually.
